solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

entries.clue: Campaign for aircraft to absorb carbon (7)

indicators.note: the aircraft soaks up the carbon, so JET takes C inside it

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

annotation.surface: A campaign in favour of planes that capture carbon, the aviation industry's green dream.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For aircraft' reads as one phrase naming who the campaign serves; the two words do separate jobs, and the carbon is only a letter taken inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A project is a planned campaign of work towards a goal.

entries.clue: Holiday island's despised colonialist (6)

blocks.note: the Greek island popular with tourists
Cecil, the Victorian empire-builder in southern Africa, now widely reviled

annotation.surface: A tourist island that happens to share its name with a hated empire-builder.
annotation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes founded Rhodesia; the 'Rhodes Must Fall' campaign made him a byword for colonialism.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhodes is both a sunny Greek island and the surname of the reviled colonialist.

entries.clue: Fair to arrest crude, disruptive group? (4,4,3)

annotation.surface: A demand that it is only fair to lock up some unruly, badly behaved gang.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crude' looks like an adjective describing the group; it is the noun, crude oil. Just Stop Oil is a UK climate-protest group known for disrupting roads and events.
annotation.definitionFit: Just Stop Oil's protests deliberately disrupt traffic and events, hence a disruptive group.

entries.clue: Rich bastard Trump's final Tweet (5)

indicators.note: a bastard version is a corrupted, impure one, so RICH is mangled
takes the last letter of Trump

annotation.surface: A jibe at a wealthy scoundrel's last social-media post.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at Trump's posts on Twitter; the definition wants a bird's tweet instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the bird's call, not the social-media post the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Integrity shown by political leader, Nick and one disheartened Tory (7)

indicators.note: the first letter of political
loses its heart, the middle letters

blocks.note: to nick is to steal, rob
TORY without its middle letters OR

annotation.surface: A sarcastic nod to the honesty of a politician named Nick and a despondent Conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital N makes Nick look like a name; it is the slang verb to steal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean steadfast moral uprightness.

entries.clue: Like Harry draws income from TV series, etc. (9)

blocks.note: a drawn game is a tie

annotation.surface: Prince Harry earning money from his Netflix show and similar ventures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draws' reads as a verb meaning earns; it is the plural noun, drawn matches.
annotation.definitionFit: Royalties are payments to creators each time their work, such as a TV series, is sold or shown.

entries.clue: see 26dn. (3)
Paper is at mischief to break Rowan? (8)

indicators.note: letters up to mischief get jumbled
the jumbled letters break into TREE, splitting it

blocks.note: a rowan is a tree; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: A newspaper stirring up trouble to damage someone called Rowan, perhaps Rowan Atkinson or Williams.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Rowan a person; it is the rowan tree, or mountain ash.
annotation.definitionFit: A treatise is an academic paper or written study.

entries.clue: Number two performer drops lead singer (6)

indicators.note: loses its leading letter, C

blocks.note: a 'number two' is a crap, so one who does it is a crapper

annotation.surface: A backing act demoted after losing its frontman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number two performer' sounds like a second-billed act; it is childish slang for someone defecating.
annotation.definitionFit: A rapper performs songs by rapping, so is a kind of singer.

entries.clue: Politicians on theft: "Intriguing activity!" (10)

blocks.note: piracy is theft, at sea or of copyrights

annotation.surface: Politicians discussing theft, calling it fascinating stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' looks like fascinating; here it means plotting.
annotation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is an intrigue, a secret plot.

entries.clue: Bass pissed about (4)

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned round, as in about-face, so the word is read backwards

annotation.surface: A drunk bass player lurching around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' reads as British slang for drunk; here it means urinated.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in music: both describe a low-pitched voice or note.

entries.clue: see 27ac. (4)
Turning up to be recruited by Opposition – not enjoyed by present government (10)

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer (a thing the government lacks) rather than naming it

indicators.note: something turning up is flipped over, so in an across clue UP is written backwards
PU is taken into the ranks of POLARITY

blocks.note: polarity = opposition, as of magnetic poles

annotation.surface: Someone showing up to be enlisted by the Opposition, a party the government's lack of favour is driving people towards.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital O makes Opposition the parliamentary party; it is the abstract noun, polarity.
annotation.definitionFit: Popularity is public approval, something the government does not currently enjoy.

entries.clue: Fit and looked after, as Republican true-believers consider themselves? (5-6)

blocks.note: to mind children is to look after them

annotation.surface: Healthy and well cared for, the way committed Republicans see themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: right-minded means sensible, and Republicans are also right-wing minded.
annotation.definitionFit: True believers think themselves right-minded, holding the correct views, and Republicans are on the political right.

entries.clue: Was a successful candidate a socialist on reflection? Miracle! (6)

indicators.note: a reflection shows RED back to front

blocks.note: a successful candidate won the election

annotation.surface: Amazement that a socialist, all things considered, actually won an election.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reads as 'thinking about it'; it is a mirror image.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a miracle is a marvel, something that makes you gasp.

entries.clue: Mayor does broadcast: expect a bad prediction from him (9)

definitions.text: expect a bad prediction from him
definitions.note: the definition is a description of the person rather than a synonym

indicators.note: the letters are scattered, like seed broadcast over a field

annotation.surface: A mayor going on air, from whom you can expect only gloomy forecasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like radio or TV; here it means scattered.
annotation.definitionFit: A doomsayer is someone who habitually predicts disaster.

entries.clue: Scoff: "All the rage gets crushed!" (6)

indicators.note: GETS is squashed out of shape

blocks.note: what is all the rage is in fashion, in

annotation.surface: Someone mocking a fashionable fury that is duly flattened.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like jeer; it is the British slang sense, to eat greedily.
annotation.definitionFit: A British slang sense: to scoff is to eat greedily, which means taking food into the body.

entries.clue: Doctor nears end – a captive of gin? (8)

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition is a noun phrase describing the state

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

annotation.surface: A doctor watching an alcoholic near the end of a life held hostage by gin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but a trap or snare, as in a rabbit gin; the question mark flags the double meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: Something caught in a gin, or snare, is ensnared.

entries.clue: Entirely a fan of Tony? Only 50% (2,4)

indicators.note: keep only half of TONY's letters

blocks.note: a fan of jazz is into jazz

annotation.surface: Asking whether someone is wholly devoted to Tony Blair, and answering only halfway.
annotation.walkthrough: In toto is Latin for 'in total', used in English to mean entirely.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Latin phrase meaning 'in total', used in English as a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Stupid arse Ted Cruz, extremely "fake" (6)

indicators.note: ARSE is in a muddled state
takes the extreme letters of Ted Cruz

blocks.note: first and last letters of TEDCRUZ

annotation.surface: An insult hurled at US senator Ted Cruz as a phoney.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stupid arse' reads as one insult; 'stupid' is the instruction and ARSE the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Ersatz means fake or an inferior substitute.

entries.clue: Pardon shagging failing to start: penis tip's stuck in shaft (6)

indicators.note: SEX loses its first letter
the tip of penis is its end letter
something stuck in a thing is lodged inside it, so the tip goes inside the shaft

blocks.note: a snooker cue is a wooden shaft

annotation.surface: A bawdy apology for sexual failure and a painful accident.
annotation.walkthrough: The tip here is the end of the word, S, not the P at its start.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to forgive a fault or let someone off.

entries.clue: Actor, one banging under piano (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, LAYER sits below P

blocks.note: a layer is one who lays, slang for having sex

annotation.surface: An actor caught in the act under a piano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banging' looks like hammering on the piano; it is slang for having sex, which is laying.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: actors were long called players, as in Shakespeare's 'merely players'.

entries.clue: Loses knack, screwing in short hose (5,5)

indicators.note: the letters are twisted round

annotation.surface: Someone losing their touch in bed while fitting a short garden hose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hose' looks like a garden pipe; it is the old word for stockings.
annotation.definitionFit: Ankle socks are short socks, and hose is an old word for leg coverings.

entries.clue: Timid type coming into the reckoning in bed? (5)

definitions.text: coming into the reckoning in bed?

blocks.clueFragment: coming into the reckoning in bed?
blocks.note: insomniacs count animals jumping a fence to fall asleep

annotation.surface: A shy person turning up in a bedtime tally.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: counting sheep is the old cure for sleeplessness, so sheep figure in the count you do in bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A sheep is a timid follower, and sheep are what you count in bed.

entries.clue: Man from Oasis left? (4)

definitions.note: Man is one example of the answer, the Isle of Man

indicators.note: the letters come out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of Oasis run into the first two of left

annotation.surface: A band member who quit Oasis, like one of the Gallagher brothers.
annotation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, a British island in the Irish Sea; the surface wants a man who left the band.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Man, the island between Britain and Ireland, is one of its kind.

entries.clue: Extreme left-winger with tense balls (4)

annotation.surface: A far-left activist whose nerves are all knotted up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is British slang for nonsense; so is rot.
annotation.definitionFit: A Trot is a Trotskyist, a far-left radical.

entries.clue: (& 7dn.) Kickback taken by a Democrat? Deplorable (3)

blocks.note: to kick is to boot, and back sends it the other way

annotation.surface: A bribe accepted by a Democrat, deemed disgraceful.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 7 down. 'Kickback' reads as one word for a bribe; it splits into kick and back.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase is said of something regrettable, which is what deplorable means.

entries.clue: (& 12ac.) Way to dance with teensy dress and old hat (10)

indicators.note: the letters dance into a new order

annotation.surface: A fashion tip to dance in a tiny frock with an antique hat.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 12 across. 'Old hat' looks like headwear; it is the idiom for something stale.
annotation.definitionFit: Yesterday's news is something no longer interesting, old hat.

entries.clue: Put off by uranium dumped in Jordan's resort (7)

indicators.note: U is thrown in with the other letters
re-sort: the combined letters are sorted again

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: A holiday resort in Jordan spoilt by nuclear waste being dumped there.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place; read it as re-sort, to sort again.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: postponing a meeting to a later date.

entries.clue: Description of web developer's spot with dire 'alternative' content (7)

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition says it describes a spider's things

indicators.note: DIRE in an alternative arrangement
the rearranged letters are the contents of SPY

annotation.surface: A review of a website designer's spot filled with awful 'alternative' material.
annotation.walkthrough: The web developer is not a coder but a spider, the creature that builds webs.
